title: The exit price signal is not a price: a fixed probe (the ETH buy amount reused as a raw token amount) is quoted, and the ratio of two quote outputs drives every exit decision

evidence.note: queryPrice quotes tokenIn=token -> WETH with amountIn = buyAmountWei (V3 quoter :325-333, V2 getAmountsOut :335-338) and returns Number(amountOut)
startExitMonitor: buyAmountWei = parseEther(buyAmountNative), i.e. the snipe size in native-coin wei, then passed as the token amountIn
entryPrice = the probe output at monitor start
pollExitStrategy: currentPrice = the same probe output each tick

priceMultiple = currentPrice / state.entryPrice: a ratio of two quote outputs, used by partial tiers (:1732), trailing activation at 2.0 (:1774), trailing trigger (:1751-1752) and stop-loss (:1782-1783)
a null quote returns continue before every check, including the 30-minute urgency exit (:1801)
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Native buy wei are used as raw token quote input
codex (22-27 independent second opinion, graded S1): Quote failure suppresses the unconditional urgency exit

sub_claims.claim: (1) Unit mismatch: the probe sells a fixed raw token amount equal to the ETH buy size in wei (for a 0.01 snipe, 1e16 raw units) whatever the token decimals: 0.01 tokens of an 18-decimal token, 10,000,000 tokens of a 9-decimal token. Its size relative to the position and to the pool varies by many orders of magnitude between tokens.
evidence: no decimals() read anywhere in the slice (sweep C03 search)
test/realpath/triage/AUD-EXIT-003.test.ts claim probe-is-eth-buy-wei-as-token-amount (plan 23-07, real path: a 9-decimal token is probed with 1e16 raw units)

sub_claims.claim: (2) Non-linear quote: for a V2 pool, out = R_out*d*0.997/(R_in + 0.997*d). The ratio at :1714 equals the spot-price ratio only when the probe d is tiny against the token reserve R_in. When d is comparable to or larger than R_in (low-decimal tokens, thin pools) the output saturates toward R_out and the ratio tracks the WETH reserve, roughly the square root of the price ratio: a 25% stop-loss then fires only near a 44% price drop and a 15% trailing stop near 28%. The same probe also makes partial-tier multiples (2x, 5x) mean different price moves per token.
evidence: constant-product arithmetic from the V2 getAmountOut formula; magnitude per real token is unmeasured

sub_claims.claim: (3) Zero or coarse output: with an 18-decimal, very-high-supply token the small probe can quote 0 or a few wei. A few-wei quote makes priceMultiple jump in large steps, so rounding alone can cross the stop-loss; a current quote of 0 with a non-zero entry gives priceMultiple 0, which fires stop-loss or trailing immediately.

(4) Non-finite ratio when entryPrice is 0 (a 0 first quote is accepted, only null is rejected at :1870). Re-measured against the code, the effect differs from the research hint ("trailing and stop-loss never fire"): current > 0 gives Infinity, which activates trailing on the first tick (:1774), disables stop-loss (:1781) and fires every partial tier at once (:1732, Infinity >= every multiple), selling the whole tier percentage immediately; current = 0 gives NaN (0/0), and stop-loss then fires because fixedStopPrice is 0 and 0 <= 0 (:1782-1783). The alert text (formatExitReason, :1665) shows NaN/Infinity.
evidence: test/realpath/triage/AUD-EXIT-003.test.ts claims zero-entry-infinite-ratio-fires-every-partial-tier and zero-entry-nan-ratio-fires-stop-loss (plan 23-07, real path: a 0 first quote is kept, Infinity sells both partial tiers, NaN fires the stop-loss)

sibling_sites_checked: Every consumer of queryPrice: startExitMonitor (:1869), resumeExitMonitor no-row branch (:1980), pollExitStrategy (:1708). Every consumer of priceMultiple: getUnfilledTiers (:1732), trailing activation (:1774), formatExitReason (:1661-1680), the partial alert (:1521). The probe amount source differs per entry: bot.ts:422 (buyAmountNative of the buy), bot.ts:1483 and :1948/:1955 and exitEngine.ts:731 (ctx.chain.snipeAmount); the consequence of that difference is AUD-EXIT-015. The anti-rug slice measures the pool by reserves, not by this probe (not re-audited here).
severity_rationale: S1, equal to the research suggestion. Sub-claims 1 and 4 are proven by the code; 2 and 3 are proven as mechanisms, but their size for real tokens needs a Phase 23 measurement, so they stay candidate. The entry stays confirmed because the defect itself (the signal is a fixed-probe output ratio, not a decimals-aware price) is a code fact. Capital class STRAND for the null-quote path (no exit at all, not even urgency); the zero/non-finite paths instead sell at the wrong time (LOSS), noted in the sub-claims.
recommendation: Replace the probe with a decimals-aware spot price (read decimals once, quote a small fixed fraction of the position or read reserves/slot0), persist the probe definition with the entry, reject a 0 or non-finite entry, and let the 30-minute urgency exit fire even when the quote is null. Decide on card EXIT-02 (Phase 24, after a Phase 23 fork measurement on real low-decimal and high-supply tokens).

triage.note: Sub-claims 1 and 4 reproduced on the real path (plan 23-07): for a 9-decimal token every exit quote's amountIn is parseEther(snipe) (1e16 raw = 10,000,000 tokens); on a 1-quadrillion-token 1 ETH pool with a 0.001 snipe the 1e15 probe quotes 0 and 0 is kept as the entry, so a 1 percent price rise reads Infinity and sells both partial tiers (50 percent) at once, and an unchanged pool reads NaN and the stop-loss sells everything on the first tick; with every exit quote refused for 31 minutes the urgency exit never fires. Sub-claims 2 and 3 need real tokens (fork).
triage.fork_question: On real tokens and pools (low-decimal tokens, very high supply 18-decimal tokens, thin pools, fee-on-transfer tokens), how far does the fixed-probe output ratio drift from the real price ratio: does the quote saturate so the ratio tracks about the square root of the price (sub-claim 2, a 25 percent stop-loss firing only near a 44 percent drop), and how coarse are few-wei quotes (sub-claim 3)?
